C4_ORTHOGONALITY.reading: Repair B is unambiguously clean: verified independent of Repair A's state (DEFEND-off/HOME-on shows the identical single legality fix with zero change to G6_TARGET's fail list), fixes exactly its one target defect, and touches nothing else. Repair A's shortfall is also independent of B (DEFEND-on/HOME-off shows the identical G3/G4 target failure), so the two repairs do not interact -- Repair A simply does not achieve its goal at these specific fixtures, for a reason found only by executing it.

WHY_REPAIR_A_DID_NOT_CLEAR_THE_GATE.not_a_vocabulary_defect: The new DEFEND_FLAG and DEFEND_OUTWARD macros are proven exact in isolation: 4 dedicated pytest known-answer tests (test_defend_flag_macro_targets_current_own_flag_pos_not_home_live_engine, test_defend_outward_macro_matches_scalar_ray_to_boundary_live_engine, test_defend_outward_zero_vector_uses_heading_fallback_live_engine, test_effective_projected_target_matches_live_engine_for_repaired_defend) all pass, each checking a single-tick, no-commitment target resolution against the live production engine bit-for-bit. The primitive itself is correct.
WHY_REPAIR_A_DID_NOT_CLEAR_THE_GATE.the_actual_cause: Native oracle oscillation at the defender_radius boundary (3.5 cells). The G3/G4 fixtures place the defender agent close enough to that boundary that, as it moves under its own DEFEND_INWARD pull, it crosses inside the radius, DEFEND_OUTWARD then pushes it back out, and the branch can flip again -- within the SAME 16-tick decision horizon this contract already uses. Any macro that HOLDS a target across ticks (a commitment, which every macro in this interface has -- the new ones inherited the default go_to horizon) necessarily lags a flipping oracle by up to its commit horizon. During that lag the true target has jumped roughly 17 cells (flag position to the far boundary), which dominates a MAX-based error metric even though the primitive matches the true target exactly during the majority of ticks.
WHY_REPAIR_A_DID_NOT_CLEAR_THE_GATE.per_tick_evidence_G3_DEFEND_FLAG_SEMANTI: err=0.0 at ticks 0-5, 8-12 (10 of 16 ticks exact); err=17.93 at ticks 6-7 only, immediately after a branch flip the committed candidate had not yet re-resolved.
WHY_REPAIR_A_DID_NOT_CLEAR_THE_GATE.per_tick_evidence_G4_DEFEND_OUTWARD_SEMA: err=0.0 at ticks 0-2, 4-9, 12-15 (13 of 16 ticks exact); err=17.0-17.12 at ticks 3 and 10-11 only, at the same kind of transition.
WHY_REPAIR_A_DID_NOT_CLEAR_THE_GATE.this_is_not_new_to_the_repair: The LEGACY GO_TO_DEFENDER_SEMANTIC_TARGET waypoint candidate shows the identical semantic_branches_seen=[DEFEND_INWARD, DEFEND_OUTWARD] flip in the ORIGINAL SEALED run (verified directly against PYQUATICUS_PORT_CONTRACT_RESULT.json). The oscillation is a property of the fixtures and the native controller, present before this repair existed. It was always partially responsible for the sealed 17.0/18.3-cell numbers; this repair did not introduce it and does not make it worse.

A_THIRD_KIND_OF_PROBLEM_NOW_VISIBLE.statement: PYQUATICUS_G6_SUBGATE_DECOMPOSITION.json separated vocabulary, legality, and dynamics. Execution surfaces a fourth, distinct from all three: reference instability at a state-dependent branch boundary. Neither a missing word (vocabulary), an illegal selection (legality), nor a cross-simulator dynamics mismatch (trajectory) -- the NATIVE oracle's own instantaneous answer is not stable near this particular geometric threshold, and no committed executor, old or new, can track an oracle that has not settled.
A_THIRD_KIND_OF_PROBLEM_NOW_VISIBLE.scope_of_this_finding: Confined to the exact G3/G4 fixtures as constructed (specific starting positions relative to a 3.5-cell radius). It says nothing about whether this oscillation is common, rare, or edge-case-only across the broader state space the 4v4 DEFEND role would actually occupy during play.
A_THIRD_KIND_OF_PROBLEM_NOW_VISIBLE.interaction_with_prior_work_noted_not_co: This is a temporal-commitment-lag-against-a-changing-intent mechanism, structurally the same SHAPE as what COMMITMENT_INTERRUPTIBILITY_INTERVENTION_V1 targeted in the CTF action-interface commitment line. But it occurs in an entirely different system (the Pyquaticus port's scripted reference oracle, not the trained-policy action interface), on a different question (is DEFEND nameable at all, not does interruptibility reduce a measured mechanism), and involves no PPO or trained policy. The two must not be cited as the same finding; they are two independent instances of a general pattern (holding a target across ticks lags a target that can move), worth remembering as a pattern but not as one result.
